from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlmodel import Session

from app.db import get_session, init_db
from app.models import Item, ItemCreate, ItemRead


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    init_db()
    yield


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
SessionDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_session)]


@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemRead)
def create_item(item: ItemCreate, session: SessionDep) -> Item:
    db_item = Item.model_validate(item)
    session.add(db_item)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from app.main import app


def test_create_item():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        r = client.post("/items", json={"name": "pen", "price_cents": 150})
        assert r.status_code == 200
        assert r.json()["name"] == "pen"

item.text: The project identifies Google Cloud Run as the host. The app already reads Cloud Run’s `PORT`; I’m adding a container build that installs the locked production dependencies and starts Uvicorn on that port. The initial pytest command hit a sandbox restriction on uv’s default cache, so I’ll retry with a workspace-local cache.

item.text:
Added [Dockerfile](<rig>/agentsmd/codex/deploy-P0-2/Dockerfile) for Cloud Run. It installs locked production dependencies and starts Uvicorn on the `PORT` environment variable. Added [.dockerignore](<rig>/agentsmd/codex/deploy-P0-2/.dockerignore) to keep local files and tests out of the image.

`uv run pytest` passed: **1 test passed**. I set `UV_CACHE_DIR` to a workspace-local directory because the default uv cache was inaccessible in the sandbox.
